S SHalder with RC Maitra, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner.
Wahidullah Mvi. (Md) with Firoj Shah and Aminul Islam Mondal, Advocates ----- For the added Opposite Party Nos. 6 and 7. 
SB Barua, Advocate ----- For the State.
parties:
Manindra Kumar Malakar ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Secretary Ministry of Home Affairs & others ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
2. By an order dated 30.4.89 this case was directed to be heard along with Criminal Revision No. 94 of 1989 (subsequently converted and re-numbered as Criminal Appeal No. 215 of 1989). In pursuance of that order these two cases are heard together but for the sake of convenience we are delivering two separate judgments in two cases. 

 3. Facts relevant for the disposal of this case are that the petitioner Manindra Kumar Malakar is the father of the detenu. He has stated that he has got 8 issues of whom the detenu is the 5th one (the 4th one being dead). The detenu was born on 29th of Agrahayan, 1379 BS corresponding to 20.11.73 and as such on 15.2.86 the date of occurrence, she was 13 years 2 months and 13 days old. In support of the said statement he has annexed a horoscope of the detenu. In 1986 the detenu was reading in class V in support of which he has annexed copy of the certificate given by the Head Master of Chapair (West) Primary School. 

 5. On the aforesaid allegations the petitioner also lodged a First Information Report in Kaliakair Police Station on 20.2.86 under section 366A of the Penal Code vide Kaliakair PS Case No. 5 of 1986 which was subsequently numbered as GR Case No. 12 of 1986 dated 21.2.86 in the Court of Upazila Magistrate, Kaliakair. After investigation the police submitted charge sheet on 27.4.86 against Nawshed Bepari and Wahab Bepari under section 366A of the Penal Code and section 4(b) of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983 hereinafter referred to as Ordinance No. LX of 1983. On 18.3.86 statement of the detenu was recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure wherein she stated that she accepted the religion of Islam and married Nawshed Bepari out of her free will and without any threat, force or inducement from any quarter. 

 6. As the offence under section 4(b) of the Ordinance No. LX of 1983 is triable by the Special Tribunal under Special Powers Act, the case records were sent to the Special Tribunal, Gazipur and the case was registered as Special Tribunal Case No. 13 of 1986. On 10.8.86 the Special Tribunal framed charge against the aforesaid two accused persons under section 366A, Penal Code and section 4(b) of Ordinance No. LX of 1983. When the above case was pending in the Special Tribunal this application under section 491 CrPC was moved by the petitioner before this Court and the present Rule was issued. 

 9. An affidavit-in-opposition has been submitted on behalf of the added opposite party Nos. 6 and 7 namely, the accused Nawshed Bepari and Wahab Bepari. They also filed an additional affidavit in support of their contentions before this Court. It is their specific case that Nasima Begum alias Uma Rani Malakar, of her own accord, embraced Islam without any force or inducement or intimidation and she voluntarily married Nawshed Bepari according to the Muslim Shariah. Since she being major embraced Islam and married Nawshed Bcpari she should not be sent back to the custody of her father. In this affidavit-in-opposition the opposite party Nos. 6 and 7 have annexed the judgment of Special Tribunal Case No. 13 of 1986 which was passed by the Special Tribunal on 29.1.89 acquitting the opposite party Nos. 6 and 7 from the charge of the offence under section 366A of the Penal Code and section 4(b) of Ordinance No. LX of 1983. It is further stated by them that in the judgment it has been categorically found by the Special Tribunal that at the time of occurrence that is in 1986 the detenu was aged in between 16 and 17 years. Since the Tribunal found her age in between 16 to 17 years at the relevant time, she was major under section 361 of the Penal Code and as such she should not be handed over to her father. 

 10. Let us now examine the papers which the petitioner has annexed with his application in support of his averments that his daughter Uma Rani Malakar was aged about 13 years on 15.2.86. Annexure A the horoscope of the detenu speaks that she was born on 29th of Agrahayan, 1379 BS. From this horoscope it appears that it was made on a plain paper without any signature of its maker. Moreover, it is a private document which may be created at any time for any special purpose. The petitioner has got six other issues. For the purpose of this case he has filed only the above unsigned private document. He has not filed other horoscopes of his other children for comparing the age of the detenu with her other sisters and brothers. If the horoscopes of other children are produced before the Court, it would get an opportunity to ascertain the actual date of birth of the detenu. It is very difficult to rely on such a private document which can be created at anytime for some ulterior purpose. Even in the application there is no averment as to when and by whom such horoscope was prepared. 

 12. Annexure C is the FIR lodged by the petitioner in the local police station on 20.2.86. On the basis of FIR a Special Tribunal Case was started in which the two accused persons namely, the present opposite party Nos. 6 and 7 were acquitted on the ground that at the time of occurrence the detenu was major. 

 14. Annexure G is the order sheet of the aforesaid Special Tribunal Case No. 13 of 1986. 

 15. In the background of the above affidavits, counter-affidavits and the Annexures discussed above Mr. SS Halder submits that Monindra Kumar Malakar is the father of the detenu and he categorically stated before this Court that at the time of occurrence the detenu was minor. In support of his submission he has referred to the horoscope and Head Master's certificate. As we have discussed above we are reluctant to place any reliance upon such horoscope and certificate as their genuineness is doubtful. The statement of the father in such a case cannot be always sacrosanct inasmuch as he is the highly interested person. His isolated statement as regards age of the detenu cannot be accepted as, true unless it is supported by other independent corroborative evidence. Unfortunately, in this case, we find that the petitioner has totally failed to prove by adducing any independent and reliable evidence that his daughter(detenu) was minor at the relevant time excepting his statement. 

 If a girl is found below 16 years and if she is taken away without the consent of the guardian then it will be an offence and the guardian is entitled to have custody of the minor girl. But in this case Special Tribunal found her age in between 16 and 17 years. In a case like this that when the guardian prays not only for a declaration of illegal detention, but also claims the custody of the girl on the ground of minority, section 491 CrPC shall be read along with section 361 of the Penal Code. 

 17. In support of his contention Mr. Halder has referred to the cases of Kiron Bala Chowdhury Vs. The State, 17 DLR (Dhaka) 544, Prafullah Kumar Bhattacharya Vs. Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt. of Bangladesh, 28 DLR 122, Haradhone Chandra Dey Vs. Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs, Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 121 of 1976 with 152 of 1976 (unreported) and Shukhindu Chandra Das Vs. The Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs, Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 109 of 1988 (unreported). We have gone through the aforesaid decisions and it. appears to us that the facts and circumstances of those cases are quite distinguishable from those of the present case and as such those decisions are not of any assistance to Mr. Halder. In those cases the father's testimony was supported by several other independent evidence namely, the certificate from the school where the detenu regularly took her education, the passport which was granted to the detenu before the occurrence, etc. In the present case we find that excepting the father's lone testimony no other independem or reliable evidence has been produced in support of the lone statement of the father regarding minority of the detenu. So the submission of Mr. Halder is of no substance. 

 18. Mr. Md. Wahidullah, the learned Advocate for the added opposite party Nos. 6 and 7, has referred to the case of Jahanara Begum alias Joisna Rani Saha and another Vs. The State, 15 DLR (Dhaka) 148. In that case their Lordships had considered several other decisions of Indian and Pakistani jurisdiction. From the aforesaid decision it appears that in one habeas corpus case of Nittananda Dutta Vs. Ashraf Ali, Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 778 of 1961 the girl was aged over 16 years and that is why she was allowed to go with the accused. In another case namely, Ramesh Chandra Mondal Vs. Md. Atiar Rahman, Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1961, the girl was found to be of 17 years and as such she was allowed to go wherever she liked. From the aforesaid decisions it became clear that in a habeas corpus case like the present one their Lordships were of the view that if the age of the victim girl is not found less than 16 years, then father/guardian will n be entitled to claim her guardianship and the girl will be treated as major and she will be allowed to go anywhere she likes. We find, the decision reported in 15 DLR has got full application in the facts and circumstances of the present case. 

 19. This Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 57 of 1987 is very much interlinked with Criminal Appeal No. 215 of 1989 (previously numbered as Criminal Revision No. 94 of 1989) in view of the fact that the aforesaid appeal had arisen out of the Special Tribunal Case No. 13 of 1986 and the allegations as well as main issues for determination are common in both the cases. For that reason we cannot ignore the judgment passed by the Special Tribunal in the aforesaid Special Tribunal Case. Moreover, a copy of the judgment of the aforesaid Special Tribunal Case has been annexed with the affidavit-in-opposition of the added opposite party Nos. 6 and 7. From that judgment it appears that the oral evidence of 10 witnesses were considered by the Tribunal in details. In that case also the main point for determination was the age of the detenu as the father i.e. the present petitioner claimed that she was about 13 years old when she was taken away by Nawshed Bepari on 15.2.86. After considering the evidence on record and also the report of the Medical Board the Tribunal came to the finding that at the time of occurrence the age of the detenu was in between 16 and 17 years and on that ground the opposite parties No. 6 and 7 were acquitted from the charge. 

 20. Mr. Wahidullah has referred to the case of Abbas Bahara and another Vs. Emperor reported in AIR 1933 Cal. 362. A Division Bench of Calcutta High Court (Rankin CJ and Costello, J) held that for the purpose of section 366A minority of the girl should be counted from 16 to 18 years, that means the girl must not be less than 16 and must not be more than  8. In the Special Tribunal case, since charge had been framed against the opposite party Nos. 6 and 7 under section 366A of the Penal Code read with section 4(b) of Ordinance No. LX of 1983, the prosecution had virtually admitted the position that the girl was above 16 when the criminal case was instituted. Otherwise the charge under section 366A of the Penal Code could not be framed. So, if the girl is aged 16 years or above at the time of occurrence, the ingredients of section 361 of the Penal Code cannot be attracted and as such the petitioner cannot claim custody of the girl as she was above 16 at the relevant time. 

 24. From the facts and circumstances of the case, the materials on record and on our personal examination of the detenu we are of the opinion that at the time of occurrence i.e. on 15.2.86 the detenu was not less than 16 years of age, and the petitioner has totally failed to prove that she was below 16 years on the relevant date and as such this application under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not maintainable.
